summary: Turns the search page into a client component. It reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and renders them as a list.

findings.title: URL query rendered as raw HTML
findings.problem: The heading injects the q search parameter into innerHTML without escaping. An attacker controls q through the link they share.
findings.consequence: A crafted search link runs attacker script in the victim's session. This is reflected XSS.
findings.fix: Render the query as a normal JSX text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Effect refetches on every render
findings.problem: The effect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each fetch calls setResults with a new array, which triggers another render.
findings.consequence: The page sends search requests in an endless loop. That loads the catalog API and keeps the browser busy.
findings.fix: Pass [query] as the effect's dependency array.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional return
findings.problem: SearchPage returns early when q is missing, before useState and useEffect run. The hook count then changes between renders when q appears or disappears.
findings.consequence: React throws a hooks-order error when the user moves between a URL with q and one without it. The page crashes.
findings.fix: Call useState and useEffect before any return. Move the empty-query check into the effect and the JSX.

findings.title: Search form removed with no replacement
findings.problem: The change deletes the only search input in the app. The empty state still tells the user to type a search term.
findings.consequence: Users who open the search page have no field to type a query into. They can search only by editing the URL.
findings.fix: Keep the form with the q input on the page, both in the empty state and above the results.

findings.title: Search failure leaves an unhandled rejection
findings.problem: searchProducts throws when the response is not ok. The promise chain has no catch handler.
findings.consequence: A failed search produces an unhandled rejection and shows the user nothing. The page shows an empty list with no error.
findings.fix: Add a catch handler that stores an error state and renders a message.

findings.title: List items lack a stable key
findings.problem: Each list item rendered from results has no key prop. Product has an id field that would serve as a stable key.
findings.consequence: React warns in the console and reconciles items poorly when results change.
findings.fix: Set key to product.id on each list item.

findings.title: New search behavior has no test
findings.problem: SearchPage now fetches and renders results from the URL query. No test in the repository covers this behavior.
findings.consequence: Regressions in fetching, the empty state or rendering will go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a component test for the empty query, the results list and a failed fetch.
